title: Early release scheme won't work without us, says ex-prisoner

evidence_packet.title: Early release scheme won't work without us, says ex-prisoner
evidence_packet.lead: Jamie Dale spent more than 11 years in prison and now runs a support network for former inmates
evidence_packet.summary: Jamie Dale spent more than 11 years in prison and now runs a support network for former inmates
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A former prisoner who runs a support network for ex-offenders said government plans to release inmates early would fail to ease prison overcrowding without support from people who had experienced the system themselves Jamie Dale, 47, from Rochdale, in Greater Manchester, spent more than 11 years in prison for his involvement in organised crime. He now runs the Old Lags Network, which aims to cut reoffending and bridge the gap between prison and the community He said many prisoners "fall through the cracks" after release "Most of the people who return quite quickly have not got great family networks," he said Dale said involving ex-offenders in developing solutions would "drastically reduce the amount of people being recalled to prison" "A lot of them can just end up sleeping on the streets," he said

title: Middleton residents campaign to keep beloved kickpitch

evidence_packet.title: Middleton residents campaign to keep beloved kickpitch
evidence_packet.lead: Residents in the Langley Estate of Middleton are campaigning to keep their community kickpitch in the area
evidence_packet.summary: Residents in the Langley Estate of Middleton are campaigning to keep their community kickpitch in the area
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Residents in Middleton are campaigning for a replacement football pitch after plans were announced to turn the existing site into a car park Campaigners say the pitch in Burnside Crescent on the Langley Estate is a community hub as well as somewhere people can play football and other sports The pitch, which is next to the Burnside Centre, is one of three on the estate, and the car park will be for the centre Families say they have been told replacement facilities will be provided at Rochdale AFC and Rochdale Council's planned Football and Community Wellbeing Hub at Bowlee Playing Fields. But they are campaigning for the new pitch to be created on land next to the original The Burnside Centre said it understands why people are disappointed to see the pitch decommissioned, but said one of the reasons the decision was made related to concerns about antisocial behaviour It added: "The pitch, which dates back to the late 1990s, had reached the end of its expected lifespan and required significant investment to remain operational."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Plot targeting Manchester Jewish community disrupted, say police - BBC News Image caption, Two suspects were detained in Manchester city centre on Sunday, police said By Lauren Hirst , North West and Lucy Manning , Special correspondent Published 22 September 2026 Two men have been arrested over a suspected terrorist plot to target the Jewish community in Manchester, police have said. The men, both in their 30s, were arrested on Sunday on the eve of Yom Kippur - considered to be the holiest day in the Jewish calendar - when thousands of British Jews were in synagogues already guarded with a heavy security and police presence. The men were detained on suspicion of offences under Section 41 of the Terrorism Act 2000, according to the Metropolitan Police, which is leading the investigation. Sources have told the BBC the suspected plot was "fairly imminent" and in the later stages of planning. Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said the government would "continue to do all in our power to address threats against our Jewish community". She added: "We cannot expect our Jewish community to live behind higher walls. "We must also tackle antisemitism at its source and root it out wherever it rears its head." 'Remain viligant' Deputy Assistant Commissioner Vicki Evans said police were aware the news would cause "further concern" to the Jewish community "especially given the significant High Holy day period". The two suspects remain in police custody after being taken to a London police station for questioning. Police said the investigation related to a "suspected terrorist plot to target the Jewish community in the Manchester area". title: Man 'paid for terrible decision with his life', inquest told

evidence_packet.title: Man 'paid for terrible decision with his life', inquest told
evidence_packet.lead: Will Place died when he crashed his car after drinking while watching a football match, an inquest finds
evidence_packet.summary: Will Place died when he crashed his car after drinking while watching a football match, an inquest finds
evidence_packet.evidence_text: An inquest jury has found that a man died after drink-driving at speeds of more than 70mph before he crashed into a pub in Heywood, Greater Manchester Will Place, 23, had been drinking in Rochdale after watching the England vs Slovakia match at Euro 2024 and got behind the wheel of his car in the early hours of 1 July 2024 When police in a marked van saw him pass a red light on Manchester Road, they immediately began following him at high speed - but officers called off the pursuit shortly before Place collided into the White Lion pub The narrative verdict made no mention about the conduct of police officers who had responded to the incident in the moments before the fatal crash The inquest jury at Rochdale Coroner's Court found that, on the balance of probabilities, alcohol played a contributing factor to Place's decision-making in the moments before he died In their verdict, the jury also found that his speed was excessive throughout the pursuit and a bend in the road contributed to the instability of the vehicle

title: Nine arrested after protest at drone factory in Staffordshire

evidence_packet.title: Nine arrested after protest at drone factory in Staffordshire
evidence_packet.lead: Staffordshire Police was called to UAV Engines, a subsidiary of Elbit Systems, on Monday
evidence_packet.summary: Staffordshire Police was called to UAV Engines, a subsidiary of Elbit Systems, on Monday
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Nine arrested after protest at drone factory in Staffordshire - BBC News Image source, Google Image caption, Staffordshire Police was called to UAV Engines, a subsidiary of Elbit Systems, in Shenstone on Monday Published 22 September 2026 Nine people opposed to Israel's military action in Gaza have been arrested after a protest at a drone factory. Police were called to UAV Engines, a subsidiary of Israeli firm Elbit Systems, in Shenstone, Staffordshire, at 06:40 BST on Monday. Four people were held on suspicion of the charge of "lock on to person/object/land to cause serious disruption". They are two men aged 57 and 73 from the Stroud area of Gloucestershire; a 39-year-old woman of no fixed address; and a 77-year-old man from the Bolton area. A man, 55, of no fixed address, was arrested on suspicion of wilful obstruction on a highway. Four others were questioned on suspicion of both offences, Staffordshire Police said. They are a 74-year-old woman from Powys, mid Wales; a 63-year-old woman from the Radstock area in Somerset, a 30-year-old woman from Basildon, Essex; and a 24-year-old woman from London. The police force said protest activity in the area had finished and inquiries were continuing. evidence_packet.evidence_text: A former prisoner who runs a support network for ex-offenders said government plans to release inmates early would fail to ease prison overcrowding without support from people who had experienced the system themselves Jamie Dale, 47, from Rochdale, in Greater Manchester, spent more than 11 years in prison for his involvement in organised crime. He now runs the Old Lags Network, which aims to cut reoffending and bridge the gap between prison and the community He said many prisoners "fall through the cracks" after release "Most of the people who return quite quickly have not got great family networks," he said Dale said involving ex-offenders in developing solutions would "drastically reduce the amount of people being recalled to prison" "A lot of them can just end up sleeping on the streets," he said

evidence_packet.summary: Residents in Middleton are campaigning for a replacement football pitch after plans were announced to turn the existing site into a car park Campaigners say the pitch in Burnside Crescent on the Langley Estate is a community hub as well as somewhere people can play football and o
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Residents in Middleton are campaigning for a replacement football pitch after plans were announced to turn the existing site into a car park Campaigners say the pitch in Burnside Crescent on the Langley Estate is a community hub as well as somewhere people can play football and other sports The pitch, which is next to the Burnside Centre, is one of three on the estate, and the car park will be for the centre Families say they have been told replacement facilities will be provided at Rochdale AFC and Rochdale Council's planned Football and Community Wellbeing Hub at Bowlee Playing Fields. But they are campaigning for the new pitch to be created on land next to the original The Burnside Centre said it understands why people are disappointed to see the pitch decommissioned, but said one of the reasons the decision was made related to concerns about antisocial behaviour It added: "The pitch, which dates back to the late 1990s, had reached the end of its expected lifespan and required significant investment to remain operational."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Two men have been arrested over a suspected terrorist plot to target the Jewish community in Manchester, police have said The men, both in their 30s, were arrested on Sunday on the eve of Yom Kippur - considered to be the holiest day in the Jewish calendar - when thousands of British Jews were in synagogues already guarded with a heavy security and police presence The men were detained on suspicion of offences under Section 41 of the Terrorism Act 2000, according to the Metropolitan Police, which is leading the investigation Sources have told the BBC the suspected plot was "fairly imminent" and in the later stages of planning Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said the government would "continue to do all in our power to address threats against our Jewish community" She added: "We cannot expect our Jewish community to live behind higher walls

title: Man 'paid for terrible decision with his life', inquest told

evidence_packet.title: Man 'paid for terrible decision with his life', inquest told
evidence_packet.lead: An inquest jury has found that a man died after drink-driving at speeds of more than 70mph before he crashed into a pub in Heywood, Greater Manchester Will Place, 23, had been drinking in Rochdale after watching the England vs Slovakia match at Euro 2024 and got behind the wheel
evidence_packet.summary: An inquest jury has found that a man died after drink-driving at speeds of more than 70mph before he crashed into a pub in Heywood, Greater Manchester Will Place, 23, had been drinking in Rochdale after watching the England vs Slovakia match at Euro 2024 and got behind the wheel
evidence_packet.evidence_text: An inquest jury has found that a man died after drink-driving at speeds of more than 70mph before he crashed into a pub in Heywood, Greater Manchester Will Place, 23, had been drinking in Rochdale after watching the England vs Slovakia match at Euro 2024 and got behind the wheel of his car in the early hours of 1 July 2024 When police in a marked van saw him pass a red light on Manchester Road, they immediately began following him at high speed - but officers called off the pursuit shortly before Place collided into the White Lion pub The narrative verdict made no mention about the conduct of police officers who had responded to the incident in the moments before the fatal crash The inquest jury at Rochdale Coroner's Court found that, on the balance of probabilities, alcohol played a contributing factor to Place's decision-making in the moments before he died In their verdict, the jury also found that his speed was excessive throughout the pursuit and a bend in the road contributed to the instability of the vehicle

evidence_packet.summary: Hosting world leaders at the G20 summit in Manchester in 2027 will give the city a "chance to shine", according to business leaders The annual gathering of the world's largest economies will take place on 27 and 28 November 2027 at the Manchester Central Convention Centre The las
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Hosting world leaders at the G20 summit in Manchester in 2027 will give the city a "chance to shine", according to business leaders The annual gathering of the world's largest economies will take place on 27 and 28 November 2027 at the Manchester Central Convention Centre The last time the summit was held in the UK was in 2009 when it was hosted in London. The cost of the security operation at the time was an estimated £7.2m Assistant Chief Constable Chris Sykes from Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said it would be a "complex and significant security operation" Sykes said the force has been planning for the event for some time, having been notified earlier this year that Manchester would be announced as the host city He said: "I am confident in our ability to deliver a safe and secure summit while continuing to meet the day-to-day policing needs of communities across Greater Manchester."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: North West health correspondent Published 22 September 2026 A row has erupted over NHS policies which allow transgender women onto women-only wards A consultant psychiatrist at Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust (GMMH) claims a patient, who identified as a trans woman, exposed themselves to female patients during their stay Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust (GMMH) said it had investigated the allegations and had no record of this ever happening The case highlights the fact that the NHS still has no national policy reflecting legal changes which say single-sex services must reflect biological sex Earlier this month, The Times reported that the psychiatrist, who has not been named, had filed a tribunal claim with the Advisory, Conciliation and Arbitration Service (Acas) in August , external She said she had raised repeated concerns with GMMH over its trans inclusion policies, which are likely to be in breach of a Supreme Court ruling given 17 months ago

title: Nine arrested after protest at drone factory in Staffordshire

evidence_packet.title: Nine arrested after protest at drone factory in Staffordshire
evidence_packet.lead: Nine people opposed to Israel's military action in Gaza have been arrested after a protest at a drone factory Police were called to UAV Engines, a subsidiary of Israeli firm Elbit Systems, in Shenstone, Staffordshire, at 06:40 BST on Monday Four people were held on suspicion of t
evidence_packet.summary: Nine people opposed to Israel's military action in Gaza have been arrested after a protest at a drone factory Police were called to UAV Engines, a subsidiary of Israeli firm Elbit Systems, in Shenstone, Staffordshire, at 06:40 BST on Monday Four people were held on suspicion of t
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Nine people opposed to Israel's military action in Gaza have been arrested after a protest at a drone factory Police were called to UAV Engines, a subsidiary of Israeli firm Elbit Systems, in Shenstone, Staffordshire, at 06:40 BST on Monday Four people were held on suspicion of the charge of "lock on to person/object/land to cause serious disruption". They are two men aged 57 and 73 from the Stroud area of Gloucestershire; a 39-year-old woman of no fixed address; and a 77-year-old man from the Bolton area A man, 55, of no fixed address, was arrested on suspicion of wilful obstruction on a highway. Four others were questioned on suspicion of both offences, Staffordshire Police said They are a 74-year-old woman from Powys, mid Wales; a 63-year-old woman from the Radstock area in Somerset, a 30-year-old woman from Basildon, Essex; and a 24-year-old woman from London The police force said protest activity in the area had finished and inquiries were continuing

evidence_packet.evidence_text: About 20 Sikh motorcyclists have taken part in a ride marking 50 years since a Manchester Sikh campaigner helped secure a change to motorcycle helmet laws The group travelled from Strangeways Prison, near Manchester city centre, to the Sikh temple Sri Guru Gobind Singh Gurdwara in the south of the city in honour of campaigner Gyani Sundar Singh Sagar Known as Gyani Ji, he spent a week in Strangeways in 1976 for refusing to pay fines for riding his moped while wearing a turban instead of a crash helmet, his son Bharat Sagar said Another son, Ujjal Singh, who was there when he was released, said returning to the spot 50 years later was "quite nostalgic" and he was proud his father's legacy lived on His sons said he got straight back on his moped after leaving prison and was stopped six more times by police within a short distance A replica of Gyani Ji's moped was displayed as riders and members of his family gathered outside the prison before setting off on the memorial ride

(Image: News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 06:06, 23 Sep 2026 Updated 07:26, 23 Sep 2026 They have flooded social media and left women facing a barrage of abuse from strangers. Yet when police tried to prosecute those responsible, nothing could be done under criminal law But could that situation change? A Liberal Democrat MP and former Rochdale councillor has opened up a significant debate on the filming and sharing of videos without consent - including the creepy ‘Manchester nightlife’ footage which is littered across the web Wera Hobhouse introduced a presentation bill on the issue to Parliament earlier this year, which fell before the summer recess. She also raised the subject during Andy Burnham ’s first day in the House of Commons as Prime Minister earlier this month Now, Ms Hobhouse has secured the backing of her party in calling for the law to be tightened so 'sexualised covert filming' and its sharing online is a criminal offence. She could also introduce a new private member’s bill to Parliament, to spark a wider debate among MPs “I think it needs a change in legislation,” Ms Hobhouse told the Manchester Evening News . “I don’t think you can ask these guys to just ‘be nice’.”

A new Bee Network report also said Avanti West Coast services were among the worst performing with cancellations doubling in July The new report, published ahead of a Bee Network committee meeting on September 24, said transport services ‘remained resilient during periods of extreme heat’. Despite the challenges , the report said it was ‘another good month’ for punctuality with both bus and Metrolink servic However rail services, which have not been taken over yet by Transport for Greater Manchester, performed worse. Problems faced included trespassing being ‘a major cause of disruption’ while crew availability continuing to be a problem All operators between June 28 to July 25 saw performance decline. Long distance operators saw the worst performance with only 42.7% of Avanti and 47% of CrossCountry trains running on time The report said Avanti was particularly hit with cancellations which more than doubled from 5.8 per cent to 12.1 pc. On asking him what was in his suitcase, he claimed he didn't pack it himself, but stated that there were a number of cigarettes inside Upon further inspection, officers discovered 16-and-a-half kilos of cannabis. In a police interview, he claimed: "It was given to me, I was just bringing it back. I ran out of money. I needed it." Eales, of Lancaster, pleaded guilty to being concerned in the fraudulent evasion of a prohibition on the importation of a class B drug, namely cannabis. evidence_packet.summary: Greater Manchester Police GMP reassures Jewish community after police stop terror attack The message comes after two men were arrested over a suspected terrorist plot to target the Jewish community in Greater Manchester Comments News Bethan Finighan S Greater Manchester Police sa
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Police GMP reassures Jewish community after police stop terror attack The message comes after two men were arrested over a suspected terrorist plot to target the Jewish community in Greater Manchester Comments News Bethan Finighan S Greater Manchester Police said there is no current "ongoing risk" to the community linked to a counter-terrorism operation as it reassured Jewish people ahead of Sukkot The force said a "robust policing presence" would continue across Greater Manchester during the Jewish High Holy Days, with dedicated patrols and an enhanced command structure in place It comes after counter terror cops from the Metropolitan Police arrested two suspects in Manchester on Sunday (September 20). The arrests were linked to an alleged threat planned against the Jewish community , the Manchester Evening News reported on Tuesday (September 22) Officers descended on Newton Street in Manchester's Northern Quarter at 2.34pm on Sunday, arresting two men on suspicion of terrorism. It was followed by a second swoop at a hostel on Lancaster Road in Salford and a raid on a flat in Liverpool Police have said they do not believe there is any ongoing threat to the public in relation to the investigation

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan Tragedy as motorcyclist killed in Wigan horror crash The road was closed off throughout the evening News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 07:25, 23 Sep 2026 View 2 Images Officers working at the scene (Image: Phil Taylor) A motorcyclist has tragically died following a crash in Wigan . Emergency services rushed out to Atherton Road, on the border of Hindley Green and Leigh , on Tuesday afternoon (September 22) Greater Manchester Police confirmed it was called out to a crash involving a car and a motorbike. It's understood the motorcyclist's next of kin have been informed following the crash Wigan council said the road was shut at the junction of Corner Lane by 5.15pm. Images from the scene showed a cordon close to the Shell petrol station, with the road closed in both directions A protective screen was erected on the road, while evidence markers were placed on the ground next to debris. A black Smart car was also seen inside the cordon Multiple police officers were pictured at the scene. It's understood the incident is being investigated by GMP's Serious Collision Investigation Unit

Then he got straight on his moped and did the very thing that landed him behind bars in the first place And the police were ready and waiting for him to do so. Between Southall Street and what is now the AO Arena the 59-year-old Sikh, known as Gyani Ji, was stopped and ticketed seven times His crime was refusing to remove his turban to wear a helmet while riding his 50cc Honda moped. And his small but persistent acts of civil disobedience would result in a landmark change in the law Gyani Ji was an activist who played a pivotal role in advancing Sikh religious rights in the UK. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester City Centre The long fightback against 'vile' nightlife videos A former Rochdale councillor is sparking a debate View 6 Images 'Manchester nightlife' videos have flooded social media in recent years - could a fightback be underway? (Image: News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 06:06, 23 Sep 2026 Updated 07:26, 23 Sep 2026 They have flooded social media and left women facing a barrage of abuse from strangers. Yet when police tried to prosecute those responsible, nothing could be done under criminal law But could that situation change? A Liberal Democrat MP and former Rochdale councillor has opened up a significant debate on the filming and sharing of videos without consent - including the creepy ‘Manchester nightlife’ footage which is littered across the web Wera Hobhouse introduced a presentation bill on the issue to Parliament earlier this year, which fell before the summer recess. She also raised the subject during Andy Burnham ’s first day in the House of Commons as Prime Minister earlier this month Now, Ms Hobhouse has secured the backing of her party in calling for the law to be tightened so 'sexualised covert filming' and its sharing online is a criminal offence. She could also introduce a new private member’s bill to Parliament, to spark a wider debate among MPs “I think it needs a change in legislation,” Ms Hobhouse told the Manchester Evening News . “I don’t think you can ask these guys to just ‘be nice’.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan Regeneration chief who oversaw controversial Astley warehouses approval to leave post Aidan Thatcher has been the driving force behind major infrastructure and inward investment projects in Wigan Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter The regeneration chief who oversaw planning approval of a controversial warehouse development in Astley has left his post Aidan Thatcher has been the borough’s director of place since 2022. One of the most senior officers at the council, he was responsible for a wide range of headline services including planning, housing, property and assets, building control, regeneration and economic development He headed the department which recommended approval of the controversial Astley warehouses development which was passed by the council’s planning committee in June 2024 Among the huge projects brought forward during his tenure are the Galleries regeneration in the town centre into the Fettlers complex, the redevelopment at Eckersley mill within the Wigan pier area and attracting more than £20m of regeneration money to transform Haigh Hall The Astley logistics park has been roundly criticised for its size and proximity to homes in Tyldesley. An independent report last year concluded that the council had followed planning processes correctly

evidence_packet.summary: Stockport Risks 'not fully appreciated' before beloved gran killed in fall from care home bedroom window A coroner has identified issues which she has ruled contributed to the tragedy View 3 Images Maureen O'Callaghan (Image: Facebook) News Chris Slater Senior Reporter 18:44, 22
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stockport Risks 'not fully appreciated' before beloved gran killed in fall from care home bedroom window A coroner has identified issues which she has ruled contributed to the tragedy View 3 Images Maureen O'Callaghan (Image: Facebook) News Chris Slater Senior Reporter 18:44, 22 Sep 2026 Updated 18:47, 22 Sep 2026 The risk a beloved gran could fall from a window at her Stockport care home was 'not fully appreciated or acted upon' - which contributed to her tragic death, a coroner has ruled Maureen O'Callaghan, who had dementia, died after falling through her upstairs bedroom window at Berrycroft Manor residential care home, in Romiley, on September 29 last year. She had repeatedly thrown items from it and previously attempted to climb out of it, an inquest into her Ms O'Callaghan moved to Berrycroft Manor in January 2025 to benefit from '24-hour care' at a cost of '£1,600 a week,' her family told South Manchester Coroner's Court last week. They said they had spoken to care home staff about safety concerns regarding the window, but nothing w Describing Ms O'Callaghan's death as a 'preventable tragedy', they said: "She was an integral part of our close family and her loss will stay with us all." View 3 Images Berrycroft Manor in Romiley (Image: Manchester Evening News)

Comme An investigation is currentl
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Transport for Greater Manchester Investigation into why power went out affecting 5,000 people on Manchester trains A new Bee Network report also said Avanti West Coast services were among the worst performing with cancellations doubling in July. Comme An investigation is currently underway into why train services across the region were thrown into chaos last month . A new Bee Network report also said Avanti West Coast services were among the worst performing with cancellations doubling in July The new report, published ahead of a Bee Network committee meeting on September 24, said transport services ‘remained resilient during periods of extreme heat’. Despite the challenges , the report said it was ‘another good month’ for punctuality with both bus and Metrolink servic However rail services, which have not been taken over yet by Transport for Greater Manchester, performed worse. Problems faced included trespassing being ‘a major cause of disruption’ while crew availability continuing to be a problem All operators between June 28 to July 25 saw performance decline. Long distance operators saw the worst performance with only 42.7% of Avanti and 47% of CrossCountry trains running on time The report said Avanti was particularly hit with cancellations which more than doubled from 5.8 per cent to 12.1 pc. CrossCountry and Transpennine Express also saw cancellations increase

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Airport He ran out of money in Bangkok, then made a huge mistake Jacob Eales has a few desperate words for police after being stopped at Manchester Airport in July View Image (Image: Greater Manchester Police) News Amy Walker Court reporter 17:36, 22 Sep 2026 A drug mule who was caught with £50,000 worth of cannabis said he got involved because he 'ran out of money' Jacob Eales, 28, was stopped by Border Force officers at Manchester Airport in July this year. On asking him what was in his suitcase, he claimed he didn't pack it himself, but stated that there were a number of cigarettes inside Upon further inspection, officers discovered 16-and-a-half kilos of cannabis. In a police interview, he claimed: "It was given to me, I was just bringing it back. I ran out of money. I needed it." Eales, of Lancaster, pleaded guilty to being concerned in the fraudulent evasion of a prohibition on the importation of a class B drug, namely cannabis. He was jailed for 22 months Sharon Leene, prosecuting, told Manchester Crown Court that on July 18 this year officers stopped Eales as he arrived on a flight back from Bangkok, Thailand, via Abu Dhabi. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester City Centre The long fightback against 'vile' nightlife videos A former Rochdale councillor is sparking a debate View 6 Images 'Manchester nightlife' videos have flooded social media in recent years - could a fightback be underway? (Image: News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 06:06, 23 Sep 2026 Updated 07:26, 23 Sep 2026 They have flooded social media and left women facing a barrage of abuse from strangers. Yet when police tried to prosecute those responsible, nothing could be done under criminal law But could that situation change? A Liberal Democrat MP and former Rochdale councillor has opened up a significant debate on the filming and sharing of videos without consent - including the creepy ‘Manchester nightlife’ footage which is littered across the web Wera Hobhouse introduced a presentation bill on the issue to Parliament earlier this year, which fell before the summer recess. She also raised the subject during Andy Burnham ’s first day in the House of Commons as Prime Minister earlier this month Now, Ms Hobhouse has secured the backing of her party in calling for the law to be tightened so 'sexualised covert filming' and its sharing online is a criminal offence. She could also introduce a new private member’s bill to Parliament, to spark a wider debate among MPs “I think it needs a change in legislation,” Ms Hobhouse told the Manchester Evening News . “I don’t think you can ask these guys to just ‘be nice’.”

Then he got straight on his moped and did the very thing that landed him behind bars in the first place And the police were ready and waiting for him to do so. Between Southall Street and what is now the AO Arena the 59-year-old Sikh, known as Gyani Ji, was stopped and ticketed seven times His crime was refusing to remove his turban to wear a helmet while riding his 50cc Honda moped. And his small but persistent acts of civil disobedience would result in a landmark change in the law Gyani Ji was an activist who played a pivotal role in advancing Sikh religious rights in the UK. One of the most senior officers at the council, he was responsible for a wide range of headline services including planning, housing, property and assets, building control, regeneration and economic development He headed the department which recommended approval of the controversial Astley warehouses development which was passed by the council’s planning committee in June 2024 Among the huge projects brought forward during his tenure are the Galleries regeneration in the town centre into the Fettlers complex, the redevelopment at Eckersley mill within the Wigan pier area and attracting more than £20m of regeneration money to transform Haigh Hall The Astley logistics park has been roundly criticised for its size and proximity to homes in Tyldesley. An independent report last year concluded that the council had followed planning processes correctly

Town hall bosses say the decision will ensure long term su Oldham Community Leisure Limited (otherwise known as Oldham Active) was appointed as the manager of the council’s leisure facilities in 2012 and this contract will end in March 2028. The company currently employs around 280 members of staff with nearly three quarters of the workf With the current model under Oldham Active coming to an end, the local authority said a review had looked at four different options. These included outsourcing services, delivering things in-house, a jointly-owned company, as well as a council-owned organisation At the moment, Oldham’s leisure services see over 1.5m visits every year with high satisfaction. Usage has been on the rise according to the report

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Transport for Greater Manchester Investigation into why power went out affecting 5,000 people on Manchester trains A new Bee Network report also said Avanti West Coast services were among the worst performing with cancellations doubling in July. Comme An investigation is currently underway into why train services across the region were thrown into chaos last month . A new Bee Network report also said Avanti West Coast services were among the worst performing with cancellations doubling in July The new report, published ahead of a Bee Network committee meeting on September 24, said transport services ‘remained resilient during periods of extreme heat’. Despite the challenges , the report said it was ‘another good month’ for punctuality with both bus and Metrolink servic However rail services, which have not been taken over yet by Transport for Greater Manchester, performed worse. Problems faced included trespassing being ‘a major cause of disruption’ while crew availability continuing to be a problem All operators between June 28 to July 25 saw performance decline. Long distance operators saw the worst performance with only 42.7% of Avanti and 47% of CrossCountry trains running on time The report said Avanti was particularly hit with cancellations which more than doubled from 5.8 per cent to 12.1 pc. CrossCountry and Transpennine Express also saw cancellations increase

On asking him what was in his suitcase, he claimed he didn't pack it himself, but stated that there were a number of cigarettes inside Upon further inspection, officers discovered 16-and-a-half kilos of cannabis. In a police interview, he claimed: "It was given to me, I was just bringing it back. I ran out of money. I needed it." Eales, of Lancaster, pleaded guilty to being concerned in the fraudulent evasion of a prohibition on the importation of a class B drug, namely cannabis. He was jailed for 22 months Sharon Leene, prosecuting, told Manchester Crown Court that on July 18 this year officers stopped Eales as he arrived on a flight back from Bangkok, Thailand, via Abu Dhabi. But the crime remains a significant issue with several boroughs seeing an increase in the last 12 months The crime has plagued Greater Manchester for decades. But police are making progress. There is evidence the force is improving in identifying and catching the often highly-organised gangs of car thieves who, at the top end, can make a lucrative living for stealing cars for export Greater Manchester Police recorded 5,303 thefts or unauthorised taking of cars, vans, and motorcycles in the year ending March 2026, compared with 5,605 for the previous year, 6,714 for 2023/24, and 8,243 for 2022/23. That equates to a fall of 35.67 percent On the basis of thefts compared to the population the riskiest area is Oldham where 706 vehicles were stolen in 2025/26 down 4.5 percent on the previous year's total of 739. This equates to 28 thefts per 10,000 residents Rochdale was next with 522 thefts, down 10.8 percent from 585, which is 22 thefts per 10,000 residents

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Three Manchester residents were among those acquitted of public nuisance today relating to blockades of dairy giant Müller during the group’s 2022 ‘Stop the Supply’ campaign The campaigners first stood trial at Worcester Crown Court in January 2025, but the jury was unable to reach verdicts on the charges that remained, and a retrial was scheduled for October 2026 but the CPS offered no evidence On 14 July 2026, the Supreme Court unanimously upheld the acquittal of six other Animal Rising campaigners who had been prosecuted for public nuisance over the blockade of the same Müller site on 8 September 2022, as part of the same ‘Stop the Supply’ campaign.[2] Rejecting an appeal by the CPS which would have overturned their acquittal, the Court ruled that people entering or leaving private business premises were not exercising a right enjoyed by the “public at large” for the purposes of the public nuisance offence under which the campa It was confirmed in court today that the prosecution was left without a viable route to conviction on the remaining public nuisance charges. The CPS offered no evidence against the six defendants, who have today been formally acquitted of all remaining charges The outcome means that campaigners involved in the 2022 actions have not only successfully defended themselves against these prosecutions, but secured a Supreme Court judgment clarifying the limits of public nuisance law and its application to actions taking place at private site

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The Greater Manchester Cancer Alliance, in partnership with The Growth Company, today launched its Get Cancer Clever Commitment, inviting employers to sign up and receive practical tools and resources to better support their employees with cancer The initiative was launched at a breakfast briefing at Manchester’s People’s History Museum, attended by around 100 senior business leaders and HR professionals from across Greater Manchester The launch follows research which found that 72% of workers in Greater Manchester felt they would find it easier to spot early cancer symptoms if their workplace shared resources, highlighting an opportunity for employers to play a greater role in helping their teams access trust The Get Cancer Clever Commitment aims to help businesses create workplaces where cancer can be discussed openly and where employees feel supported, whether they are concerned about their own health, facing a cancer diagnosis or supporting a loved one The event featured a keynote speech from Professor Chris Brookes MBE, Chairman of Wigan Warriors, followed by a panel discussion bringing together prominent members of the Greater Manchester business community, NHS clinicians and people with lived experience of cancer The morning concluded with a question-and-answer session, before attendees were invited to sign the Get Cancer Clever Commitment and take practical steps towards becoming a Cancer Clever Employer

They are two men aged 57 and 73 from
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Police were called to UAV Engines, a subsidiary of Israeli firm Elbit Systems, in Shenstone, Staffordshire, at 06:40 BST on Monday Four people were held on suspicion of the charge of "lock on to person/object/land to cause serious disruption". They are two men aged 57 and 73 from the Stroud area of Gloucestershire; a 39-year-old woman of no fixed address; and a 77-year-old man from the Bolton area A man, 55, of no fixed address, was arrested on suspicion of wilful obstruction on a highway. Four others were questioned on suspicion of both offences, Staffordshire Police said They are a 74-year-old woman from Powys, mid Wales; a 63-year-old woman from the Radstock area in Somerset, a 30-year-old woman from Basildon, Essex; and a 24-year-old woman from London The police force said protest activity in the area had finished and inquiries were continuing Follow BBC Stoke & Staffordshire on BBC Sounds , Facebook , X and Instagram

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Robert Lloyd, now 53, was part of a group of masked men who attacked Michael McDermott, 26, at his relative's home in Moston, Manchester, on 9 November 1994 Armed with baseball bats and knives, the offenders burst through the front door of the property at about 22:30 GMT. They inflicted several injuries on McDermott, including stab wounds, as he lay on the sofa Lloyd was jailed at Manchester Crown Court for a minimum of 17 years in March, but reporting restrictions had previously been in place due to ongoing police inquiries Following the attack at the house in Ashville Terrace, the group ran across the road to an alleyway and on to Oakville Terrace to a waiting vehicle which then drove them from the scene The case was reopened by Greater Manchester Police's major investigation team last October after Lloyd, from Denton, Tameside, confessed He subsequently pleaded guilty to the charge of murder in March

title: Rusholme: More than 20,000 prescription drugs seized

evidence_packet.title: Rusholme: More than 20,000 prescription drugs seized
evidence_packet.lead: Greater Manchester Police said officers stopped a man they said was acting suspiciously on Park Crescent in Rusholme on Monday evening After his arrest, officers searched a property linked to the investigation and recovered what they believe were more than 20,000 prescription dru
evidence_packet.summary: Greater Manchester Police said officers stopped a man they said was acting suspiciously on Park Crescent in Rusholme on Monday evening After his arrest, officers searched a property linked to the investigation and recovered what they believe were more than 20,000 prescription dru
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Police said officers stopped a man they said was acting suspiciously on Park Crescent in Rusholme on Monday evening After his arrest, officers searched a property linked to the investigation and recovered what they believe were more than 20,000 prescription drugs, including diazepam, pregabalin and tramadol Police also seized cannabis, ecstasy tablets and £2,300 in cash Two men in their 20s were arrested on suspicion of possessing Class A, B and C drugs with intent to supply and remain in custody Chief Insp Rob MacGregor said officers had recovered a "substantial quantity of suspected illegal drugs" following the initial arrest He said the illegal supply of drugs could have a "devastating impact" on communities and added that the investigation was continuing

title: Manchester Northern Quarter counter-terror arrests

evidence_packet.title: Manchester Northern Quarter counter-terror arrests
evidence_packet.lead: The pair were held in Newton Street at 14:45 BST on Sunday as part of an ongoing operation.
evidence_packet.summary: The pair were held in Newton Street at 14:45 BST on Sunday as part of an ongoing operation. They remain in custody Police said a property on Epworth Street in Liverpool had been searched as well as one on Lancaster Road in Salford The operation was led by the Metropolitan Police
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The pair were held in Newton Street at 14:45 BST on Sunday as part of an ongoing operation. They remain in custody Police said a property on Epworth Street in Liverpool had been searched as well as one on Lancaster Road in Salford The operation was led by the Metropolitan Police and backed up by officers from Greater Manchester Police (GMP) A Counter Terrorism Policing London spokesperson said: "Both males were arrested under Section 41 of the Terrorism Act 2000 "The operation was led by Counter Terrorism Policing London, working closely with Counter Terrorism Policing North West and Greater Manchester Police." They added: "At this time, there is no information to suggest any wider threat to the public."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Fly-tipping offences could face tougher penalties under new plans from Manchester City Council, which is proposing to increase Fixed Penalty Notices (FPNs) for serious cases to the maximum amount Offenders caught committing fly-tipping offences will now face a £1,000 fine, an increase from the current £700 penalty. Those who pay within 10 days will be eligible for a reduced payment of £700, with the full amount payable within 14 days. The landmark decision is subject to a The move is part of a wider commitment to tackle environmental crime and support the ambitions set out in Manchester's new Fly-tipping and Litter Strategy, which aims to reduce fly-tipping incidents by a third by 2035 Residents have repeatedly said cleaner streets, well-kept parks and action on environmental crime as among their top priorities for the city. Fly-tipping continues to place a significant burden on council resources, drain public money away from essential services and impact the h In 2025-26, Manchester recorded 17,954 fly-tipping incidents, resulting in the removal of more than 5,594 tonnes of waste from across the city. A total of 992 fines were issued for waste deposits in the same period The strategy supports the aims of the council's Our Manchester Strategy , which sets out a vision for cleaner, greener and better maintained neighbourhoods

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan Council has announced that it intends to appoint Acumen Waste Services Limited to clear the illegal waste site at Bolton House Road in Bickershaw, subject to contract Over the past few weeks, the council has been leading the procurement process to find the most suitable contractor to clear the entire site, with applicants asked to explain how they will safely remove the waste and manage associated risks Following the robust tender process, Acumen Waste Services Limited has been chosen as the preferred contractor. There will now be a compulsory standstill period and the contract is expected to be signed in early October, with mobilisation to remove the waste planned to start in l Councillor Paul Kenny, portfolio holder for planning, environmental services, and transport, said: “The scale of the illegal waste site at Bolton House Road has had a devastating impact on the local community, so I am delighted that we are now in a position to appoint a contracto “The appointment is a significant milestone, but residents should have never been put into this position, and we will continue to support the Environment Agency’s criminal investigation to punish those responsible for this environmental destruction.” Following an emergency response to a fire that broke out and lasted for several days in July 2025, a multi-agency partnership group was set up to manage the illegal waste site, prevent further waste deposits, and minimise the impact on the public and the environment

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Sat 26th Sep, 2026 - Sankeys Sankeys re-opening party with Low Steppa Sankeys, Sidney St, Manchester M1 7HB Sat 26th Sep, 2026 Go to Manchester's Finest X profile Sankeys Manchester kicks off its Autumn/Winter season on Saturday 26 September, returning to its new permanent home on Sidney Street with Low Steppa, Pirate Copy and Mike Morrisey B2B Luca606 taking over the opening party It marks the start of the club’s first full season back in Manchester since its much-loved Ancoats venue closed in 2017. The new 500-capacity space keeps the stripped-back, music-first approach Sankeys built its name on, but arrives this autumn with a few changes behind the scene Carved out of the former green room, Room 2 is a smaller, clandestine space designed for close-up sets and a slightly different pace from the main room. Moving the artist dressing rooms upstairs has opened up more space downstairs too, while the club’s LED matrix installation ret The music remains firmly rooted in underground house, with Sankeys deliberately keeping much of its weekly programming under wraps until closer to each event. After the opening party, the season will bring the likes of Arapu, George Smeddles, Paisley Jensen, Richy Ahmed, Darius S There’s also a Seb Zito B2B Rossko set among the dates lined up between September and mid-December, with further special guests still to be announced

There’ll be live performances, hands-on-experiences and history re-enactors all designed to make history come alive. Free to attend, you can also expect birds of prey and specialist stalls as well as activities such as scriptorium (medieval blogging), and shield and sword design for younger visitors. It already has a strong tech base and devolution gives us a chance to align policy, funding and delivery more closely with what is happening on the ground To do that well, Combined Authorities and others need to understand that ecosystems are much broader and deeper than most public-facing institutions realise, that matters if they are going to make good decisions on skills, infrastructure, procurement and innovation support AI and emerging technologies clearly need focus because their impact will be felt across every part of the economy, but policy needs to keep pace with how those technologies are being used by businesses. Government and Combined Authorities will have more impact if they understand The new Digital Campus in Manchester is a good example of where this could become practical; a larger concentration of public sector digital capability in Manchester should create new routes for startups and scaleups to work with the government. evidence_packet.evidence_text: The best industry experiences don’t just show young people what a career in tech could look like - they give them the opportunity to become part of it That’s exactly what Hippo helped create through their support of Manchester Digital’s T Connect programme, providing students with exposure to the industry, practical experience and the confidence to take their next steps into tech Hippo’s involvement began with a problem-solving session for T Connect students, where their team ran activities designed to encourage creative thinking, collaboration and approaching challenges in the way technology teams do every day Following this session, Hippo selected two learners - Ahmed Abdul Karim and Edu Samuel Manuel - to take part in a 36-day industry placement with the business The placement gave Ahmed and Edu the opportunity to work alongside Hippo’s teams from their Leeds office, contributing to projects for the Department for Education and gaining first-hand experience of working in a professional technology environment Throughout their placements, they were treated as members of the team, gaining insight into the full process of delivering digital products - from technical development and problem solving through to collaboration and communication

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained.
